MINUTES
  PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION MEETING
  JULY 16, 2024

  1.  CALL MEETING TO ORDER

  An adjourned meeting of the Park and Activities Commission of the City of Rolling Hills
  Estates was called to order at 6:02 p.m. at Highridge Park, 29035 Highridge Rd., Rolling
  Hills Estates, California, by CHAIR MCCORMICK.

  2.  SALUTE TO THE FLAG

  CHAIR MCCORMICK led those present in the Pledge of Allegiance.

  3.  ROLL CALL

  Commissioners Present:  Pope, Ciarolla, Johnson, Bain, Persichina, and
  McCormick

  Commissioners Absent:  Holdsworth

  City Staff Present:  Maintenance Superintendent Mike Goldsmith
  Community Services Supervisor Rosa Pinuelas
  Community Services Coordinator Matt Morrow

  4.  APPROVAL OF MINUTES

  A.  PARK & ACTIVITIES COMMISSION MEETING DRAFT MINUTES OF JUNE 18,
  2024

  COMMISSIONER BAIN made a motion, seconded by VICE CHAIR
  PERSICHINA to:

  APPROVE THE PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION MINUTES OF
  JUNE 18, 2024.

  There being no objection, CHAIR MCCORMICK so ordered.

  5.  AUDIENCE ITEMS

  NONE.

  6.  BUSINESS ITEMS

  A.  PENINSULA HOLIDAY PARADE MANAGEMENT PROFESSIONAL SERVICES
  AGREEMENT

PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION MEETING MINUTES  1
July 16, 2024
   Supervisor Pinuelas gave a brief overview of the proposed Peninsula Holiday
  Parade management service agreement for the 2024 Peninsula Holiday Parade of
  Lights to be held on December 7, 2024 (as per the agenda material).

  Supervisor Pinuelas stated that the company used prior to the 2023 parade did not
  respond to any correspondence to continue management services from Staff
  leading up to the 2023 parade and that Staff recommends continuing to work with
  Soundskilz, Inc., in response to COMMISSIONER POPE.

  Supervisor Pinuelas confirmed that the lighting, sound and stage are not provided
  by the parade management consultant, in response to COMMISSIONER POPE.

  COMMISSIONER BAIN asked if Staff could do more outreach to the community
  groups and clubs in the surrounding areas to be part of the parade. Staff responded
  that they could reach out to more organizations and that the COMMISSION could
  let Staff know if there were any specific organizations they would like Staff to reach
  out to.

  Supervisor Pinuelas stated that the contract specifies that in the event of
  cancellation or termination of the parade by the City for any reason, the City agrees
  to pay Soundskilz for services incurred prior to cancellation, including inclement
  weather-related cancellations, in response to VICE CHAIR PERSICHINA.

  VICE CHAIR PERSICHINA made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER
  POPE TO APPROVE AS FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

  RECOMMENDATION TO CITY COUNCIL TO ENTER INTO A
  PROFESSIONAL SERVICES AGREEMENT APPROVED AS TO FORM
  BY THE CITY ATTORNEY WITH SOUNDSKILZ, INC. TO PROVIDE
  PARADE MANAGEMENT SERVICES FOR THE PENINSULA HOLIDAY
  PARADE OF LIGHTS DECEMBER 7, 2024.

  AYES:  Pope, Ciarolla, Johnson, Bain, Persichina, McCormick
  ABSENT:  Holdsworth

  7.  STAFF ITEMS

  A.  HILLS ARE ALIVE RACE UPDATE (VERBAL REPORT)

  Coordinator Morrow gave a brief update about the 2024 Hills Are Alive Race
  including information regarding registration, marketing, sponsorships, and day of
  race event activities.

  Coordinator Morrow stated that there were 236 participants at the 2023 race, in
  response to COMMISSIONER POPE.

  B.  CONCERT IN THE PARK UPDATE (VERBAL REPORT)

PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION MEETING MINUTES  2
July 16, 2024
   Coordinator Morrow gave a brief update about the Concert in the Park event. He
  noted that the event is scheduled on Saturday, August 17 at Ernie Howlett Park
  and that country band Jasmine Fields will be performing at this year’s event. He
  also noted that the Wetzel Pretzel food truck will be providing food and drink for
  purchase.

  Coordinator Morrow stated that Staff felt that there were approximately 200 people
  in attendance at last year’s concert and that there was an 80’s cover band, in
  response to COMMISSIONER POPE.

  Coordinator Morrow stated that marketing has included social media posting, and
  that Staff will be posting flyers at the parks, in response to CHAIR MCCORMICK.

  COMMISSIONER POPE suggested placing a QR code on the flyers and a link on
  the City website to the band’s website for people to get more information and listen
  to some of their music prior to the event.

  Supervisor Pinuelas noted that there is a possibility of getting more food trucks,
  but that most require a specific revenue amount to be gained at the event. She
  stated that the Wetzel food truck does not require any upfront payment and was
  very satisfied after last year’s event, in response to COMMISSIONER BAIN.

  Staff noted that they are open to looking into local service groups providing food
  as a fundraiser option at future concerts, in response to CHAIR MCCORMICK.

  C.  MATTERS OF INTEREST (VERBAL REPORT)

  NONE.

  8.  COMMISSION ITEMS

  A.  ADOPT-A-PARK (VERBAL REPORT)

  VICE CHAIR PERSICHINA reported that the Palos Verdes Peninsula Association
  of Realtors Annual Softball Tournament that was held at Ernie Howlett Park at the
  end of June appeared to have another great turnout and that they did a very good
  job of cleaning up after the event.

  B.  MATTERS OF INTEREST (VERBAL REPORT)

  NONE.

  9.  MATTERS OF INFORMATION

PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION MEETING MINUTES  3
July 16, 2024
   A.  CITY COUNCIL ACTIONS OF JUNE 11, 2024

  RECEIVED AND FILED.

  B.  CITY COUNCIL ACTIONS OF JUNE 25, 2024 ADJOURNED MEETING

  RECEIVED AND FILED.

  C.  CITY COUNCIL ACTIONS OF JUNE 25, 2024

  RECEIVED AND FILED.

  10.  FUTURE AGENDA ITEMS

  A.  ASSESSMENT OF SPACE FOR POTENTIAL DOG PARK AND FUTURE PARKS

  Staff stated that there are issues at the majority of City parks regarding dogs being
  off leash, in response to CHAIR MCCORMICK.

  **CHAIR MCCORMICK LEFT THE MEETING AT 6:26 PM**

  11.  PARK TOURS

  A.  HIGHRIDGE PARK

  Supervisor Pinuelas gave a brief overview of an area that has potential as a
  possible location for a dog run at Highridge Park in the far outfield area of the
  softball field near the second soccer field where the frequent off leash dog issues
  continue to occur.

  COMMISSIONER JOHNSON asked whether the proposed location of the dog run
  would cause any issues with the homes and homeowners that surround the
  perimeter of the park. Supervisor Pinuelas stated that is something Staff is taking
  into consideration and the proximity of homes could cause some challenges if
  there were a dog run at Highridge Park.

  Coordinator Morrow gave a brief overview of the second area behind the first
  soccer field that has been considered as a possible location for a dog run at
  Highridge Park. A discussion ensued regarding the lack of good possible locations
  at Highridge Park as there did not appear to be a location that would not present
  challenges related to the homes that surround the perimeter of the park.

  A discussion ensued regarding other possible locations for dog runs at other City
  parks and City owned areas.

PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION MEETING MINUTES  4
July 16, 2024
   12.  ADJOURNMENT

  VICE CHAIR PERSICHINA ADJOURNED THE MEETING AT 6:52 PM TO THE
  NEXT PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION MEETING ON AUGUST 20, 2024,
  AT 6:00 P.M., WHICH WILL BE HELD AT LINDEN H. CHANDLER PRESERVE.

  There being no objection, so ordered.

  Respectfully submitted,  Approved,

  __________________________  __________________________
  Matt Morrow  Ryan McCormick
  Community Services Coordinator  Chair, Park & Activities Commission

PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION MEETING MINUTES  5
July 16, 2024
